Who we are

We use Play and Play Theory to change how people experience the places they visit, the way they work and the communities they belong to.

Beth Cooper
Play & Project Lead
Thirty years moving between performance, play theory and practice. Trained under Perry Else, one of the UK’s leading thinkers on play, and has advised the National Trust and the Royal Parks.
Dr Claudia Bordogna
Play theory in business
Senior leader at Nottingham Business School with a PhD and a background in live brand events. Brings play theory into business to lift creativity, innovation and wellbeing.
Dirk Mischendahl
Commercial & Strategy Lead
Three decades building companies where culture meets commerce: founder of Logistik, co-founder of the Northern Art Prize and former CEO of The Tetley.
Jon Eden
Production & Delivery Lead
Four decades in live events and large-scale production, from touring with major music acts to leading an events business of more than seventy people.

Places

We turn visits into experiences people stay for, spend in and come back to.

Most venues do not have a footfall problem. They have an experience problem. We audit the space, put the right play in the right place and bring it to life.

Play here means

Hands-on engagement with a place that people find for themselves, without a member of staff explaining it.

Measured by
Dwell timeSecondary spendRepeat visitsNew audiences
Who we work with
HeritageMuseumsArt galleriesVenuesParksFestivals

Work

We find where rigidity is costing your organisation time and performance, and build room to test, learn and adapt within clear guardrails.

Play is not the product. Better decisions, faster learning and adaptive performance are.

Play here means

Functional play built into the work itself: experimenting, prototyping and challenging ideas. Not away days or forced fun.

Measured by
Time to decisionTime to test an ideaReworkIdeas put into practice
Who we work with
Corporate consultancyWorkplace play auditsOffice play installationsTeam days & play sessions

Belonging

We create shared play that brings people together across age, ability and background, and builds the connections communities rely on.

Quality, artist-led play should not be kept for flagship venues. We design for access from the start, so the people most often left out are the people it is made for.

Play here means

Regular, shared and inclusive play that gives people a reason to gather and an easy way to connect.

Measured by
Who takes partHow often they returnHow connected and well people say they feel

Community projectsLocal authoritiesHousing associationsSEND commissionsEducationEDICharity
